findings.title: Embedded post author link colour flipped from 30% to 70% lightness in light themes
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original value for light themes and uses the complement for dark ones. Here the arguments are swapped: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. As a result, `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` becomes much paler in light themes. It should be `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

findings.title: custom-message-length colour inverted for light themes
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for light themes and `$secondary 70%` for dark. The values were swapped, so this hint text becomes much darker on mobile light themes. The desktop version keeps 70%/30%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Topic map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original `.topic-map h3` colour was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The conversion uses 50%/50%, which changes the existing light-theme appearance. The PR is only meant to add a dark variant. It should be `(…$primary 20%, …$secondary 80%)`, matching the desktop file.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses 50%/50%, which lightens member names in light themes. This is an unintended visual regression. It should be `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This has the same error as in the desktop user.scss file. The original value of 30% was replaced with `dark-light-choose(…50%, …50%)`, which changes the light-theme colour. It should be `(…$primary 30%, …$secondary 70%)`.

findings.title: Missed conversion: categories badge-notification still uses $primary only
findings.body: The rule `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification { color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) }` was left unconverted. In dark themes this produces the low-contrast colour this PR is trying to fix. It should be wrapped in `dark-light-choose` like the identical rules elsewhere in the PR.
